definition: Cunning means clever in a deceptive way.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cunning. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cunning should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Advertisers count on a certain cunning in shelf placement, setting the sugary cereal exactly at a six-year-old's eye level.
Clever is milder than cunning — clever praises the quickness of a mind and says nothing at all about honesty.
Scheming goes further than cunning: cunning may live inside a single trick, while a scheming rival runs a whole campaign of them.

Crafty means tricky in a patient, workshop way — the crafty player builds a trap over many turns and waits for it to spring. Cunning is the broader word for cleverness with deceit folded in: a cunning stroke may take a single moment, while craftiness suggests slow, tinkering preparation.

Sly is quieter and sneakier than cunning — sly work happens in the corners, in winks and side deals, hoping never to be noticed at all. Cunning can operate in plain sight, running its trick right in front of you while steering your attention somewhere else.

The common cuckoo never builds a nest, never broods an egg, and never feeds a chick.
Other birds do all of it for her.
Her method is a study in cunning.
She watches a reed warbler's nest for days, waits for the ten minutes when both owners are away, and lays a single egg that mimics theirs down to the speckling.
The forgery works in plain sight: the warblers return, count nothing amiss, and settle over the intruder's egg with their own.
Naturalists once assumed the trick required luck.
Timed observations showed the opposite — the cuckoo's visit lasts, on average, nine seconds.
It is hard not to admire the economy of it: one patient watcher, one perfect fake, and a season's parenting handed off to strangers.
